trust_decision.summary: WS-Fed SignInRequest.parse decides whether the caller-supplied wreply is an allowed return URL by requiring the same scheme+netloc as the provider's configured acs_url and a path prefix; the signed token is then auto-posted to wreply. At the pinned commit this origin check is ALREADY PRESENT.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the wreply origin check in WS-Federation sign-in; this is the only place wreply is validated.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Not applicable: the listed fix commit makes no source change, and the pinned tree already contains the wreply origin check.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: wreply on the same origin with a deeper path under acs_url must be accepted, and an empty wreply falls back to acs_url

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second, copy-pasted wreply parse for sign-out that a maintainer might leave without the origin check (it is currently stored in the plan context but never redirected to).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: SignOutRequest duplicates SignInRequest's parse logic, so a sibling that drifted from it would look like normal duplication.

O9_family: open redirect / return-URL validation (CWE-601) leaking a signed token

O10_build.project_tests: authentik/enterprise/providers/ws_federation/tests/test_sign_in.py:38-49 (test_wreply already covers the cross-origin suffix case)

j.j_sites_touched: none (the fix diff touches only version strings and schema.yml security annotations)

out_of_scope_notes: The fix diff's only non-version change adds `security: - {}` to four endpoints paths in schema.yml (fix.diff:131-165); that belongs to the endpoints API docs, not WS-Fed.
The remaining wreply check uses a path prefix without a segment boundary (sign_in.py:61), so '/acs' also allows '/acs-other'. That stays on the same origin, so it is not a cross-origin redirect.
